constrained_loop.builder_position: The agent loop is deliberately constrained: the orchestrator controls turn count, context assembly, follow-up triggers, and stopping conditions. The LLM reasons but does not steer. Rationale: cost governance (~$0.003/commit vs unbounded open loops), reproducibility (same commit → same deterministic context bundle), and separation of concerns (harness controls, LLM reasons). Trade-off acknowledged: an open loop might achieve higher D2/D3 by requesting blame or specific files. Deferred because D6=0.85 shows the pre-assembled bundle is sufficient for grounding; tool use is the iter-4 escalation path if D2 remains stuck.
constrained_loop.evaluator_critique: Partially justified, badly evidenced. Cost caps and oracle-safe reproducibility are real wins for batch eval at n=50+. But the builder uses D6=0.85 as proof the bundle is *sufficient* — that is a category error. D6 measures whether claims cite real diff artifacts, not whether the agent had enough information to infer failure mechanisms or defect loci. The documented failure signature (D6↑ + D3↓ + D2↓) is exactly 'reads the diff well, reasons poorly' — which is consistent with *under-contextualized* investigation, not over-contextualized noise. A constrained loop is the right V1 default, but the builder understates what is lost: (1) no selective deepening — agent cannot pull test files when behavior is defined there, not in the diff; (2) no blame/history on demand — only last-3-commits-per-file statically, which may miss the introducing change; (3) no cross-file caller/callee traversal when the bug is at an integration boundary; (4) follow-up context is orchestrator-scripted, not agent-directed, so turn 2 may inject blame when the real gap was 'show me the test that exercises this path.' The 'reopen at iter-4' timeline is too late: D2=0.08 and D3=0.13 are already catastrophic; waiting until prompt iterations fail on D2 specifically ignores that localization and diagnosis failures may share a missing-context root cause, not a prompt root cause.
constrained_loop.recommendation: Keep constrained loop for V1, but stop claiming D6 validates context sufficiency. Add a deterministic 'context gap' forensics tag in eval (e.g., commits where reasoning mentions tests/mocks/callers but bundle lacked them). Move selective context expansion (not full open agent) to iter-2 parallel track if iter-1 prompt changes lift D3 <0.18 on n=20. Consider open/semi-open loop only after controlled bundle-expansion experiments plateau.
constrained_loop.evidence_needed: Per-commit forensics classifying D3=0 failures into 'prompt-hedging' vs 'missing auxiliary context' buckets. Compare D2/D3 on n=20 with (a) current bundle, (b) bundle + auto-injected test files for touched modules, (c) bundle + blame on top-2 localized hunks. If (b) or (c) lift D2/D3 ≥0.05 without D6 regression, the constraint — not the prompt — was the bottleneck.

model_strategy.builder_position: Single model (`claude-sonnet-4-6` via Cursor SDK) for investigation (turn 1), follow-up (turns 2–3, untested), and D3/D5 judging. Rationale: best available reasoning quality on a single-shot turn; shared provider simplifies ops. Open questions note same-model judging may cause self-evaluation bias, but counter that rubric-based scoring with explicit criteria may keep bias low. Follow-up turns might use a cheaper model (turn 2 is 'commit to HIGH or LOW') but counter that uncertain cases need reasoning quality most. Cursor SDK plan mode has no native tool calling; D6=0.85 without tools suggests context assembly is sufficient.
model_strategy.evaluator_critique: Same model for investigator and judge is defensible for engineering convenience, not for measurement validity. D3 is an LLM-as-judge rubric scoring the investigator's mechanistic reasoning — when both roles share weights and stylistic priors, you risk correlated leniency: fluent, well-structured non-mechanisms (exactly the D6↑ D3↓ pattern) may score higher than they should. D5 has the same problem. The spike's b4c933b7 case (D3=1.0, D1=0.0) proves the judge can reward strong diagnosis while classification fails — it does NOT prove the judge is unbiased; it may prove the judge over-rewards articulate reasoning independent of verdict consistency. Self-evaluation bias is not hypothetical: literature on LLM-as-judge consistently shows same-family evaluator–generator pairs inflate scores 5–15% vs cross-model panels. The builder's rubric counterargument helps but does not eliminate style-matching — the rubric still requires subjective judgment on 'captures failure mechanism.' For follow-up turns, using a cheaper model on uncertain cases is backwards: uncertainty after turn 1 is when deeper reasoning is needed, not binary classification theater. Sonnet for single-turn investigation is reasonable given cost, but the claim that D3 failure is purely method/calibration (not capability) is under-tested — D3=0.13 on n=5 is far below gate and the n=100 D3 histogram is bimodal (21 commits at 0.0). A reasoning-heavy model (o1-style, Opus) might lift the long tail, but at 3–10× cost; that trade is unknowable without a controlled subset eval. Opus is unlikely to fix D1 hedging alone (spike shows identical reasoning text with different risk labels when label leaked) — rubric + mechanism floor is the right first lever — but Opus/reasoning models may matter for commits where mechanism inference requires multi-step simulation the current prompt cannot force.
model_strategy.recommendation: Split judge from investigator before n=50 acceptance: minimum bar is different provider OR different model tier for D3/D5 (e.g., investigator Sonnet, judge Opus or GPT-4.1 with adversarial judge prompt). Run same-model vs cross-model judge on n=20 and report score delta + rank correlation. Keep Sonnet for turn 1 during iter-1/2; defer Opus A/B to a 10-commit 'hard subset' (D3=0 on baseline, high D6) to bound cost. Do NOT downgrade follow-up turn model — if anything, turn 2 should be same or stronger model when triggered by low confidence.
model_strategy.evidence_needed: Judge swap experiment: same n=20 reports scored by (1) Sonnet judge [current], (2) cross-model judge, (3) 5 human ratings on rubric. Report Pearson/Spearman correlation and mean score shift. Investigator model A/B: Sonnet vs Opus on 10-commit hard subset, measure ΔD3 and cost per commit. Self-bias proxy: correlate investigator confidence with judge D3 score holding D6 fixed — positive correlation suggests leniency.

multi_turn.builder_position: Multi-turn is designed (max 3 turns, deterministic follow-up triggers: confidence <0.6, empty localization, explicit uncertainty) but V1 eval runs max_turns=1 for cost control. Improvement cycle prioritizes prompt/method quality at turn 1 (iter-1, iter-2) before enabling turns (iter-3). Escalation: if iter-2 n=50 shows D1/D3 still below gate with best single-turn method, enable turn 2 for low-confidence commits (~40% cost increase). Follow-up injects targeted questions plus deeper blame/history.
multi_turn.evaluator_critique: The 'fix turn 1 first' sequencing is disciplined project management, not a validated hypothesis about failure causality. The builder implicitly assumes D1/D3 failures are calibration/prompt problems solvable in one shot. Evidence partially contradicts this: (1) D6=0.85 means turn 1 already consumes the bundle effectively — adding prompt structure helps, but cannot inject information absent from turn 1 context; (2) multi-turn follow-up is designed to inject blame and 'what failure mode?' prompts, yet has NEVER been measured — the team may spend two full iteration cycles optimizing a single-turn local optimum while the designed turn-2 path sits idle; (3) f897d46/90846b5 cross-run proof shows reasoning text unchanged when label removed — only risk_level flips — suggesting D1 is rubric/commitment failure, which iter-1 targets, but D3=0.13 suggests many commits never reach mechanistic reasoning at all, which staged CoT addresses — however, for behavioral defects, 'what failure mode?' without test/caller context may still yield generic answers on turn 2, wasting 40% cost for marginal gain. D6=0.85 is NOT an argument against multi-turn; it is orthogonal. Multi-turn ROI is unknowable while max_turns=1 is hardcoded in eval — the builder is optimizing a subsystem that is not the production-designed loop. The 40% cost estimate assumes selective triggering; if iter-1 increases hedging and lowers confidence scores, follow-up triggers may fire MORE often, inflating cost beyond projection.
multi_turn.recommendation: Run an early multi-turn ablation in parallel with iter-1, not after iter-2 failure. Minimum design: n=20 stratified, same iter-1 prompt, max_turns=1 vs max_turns=3, measure ΔD1/ΔD3/Δcost and follow-up trigger rate. If multi-turn shows ≥0.05 lift on D3 OR ≥0.05 on D1 with ≤60% cost increase, merge into iter-2 validation rather than deferring to iter-3. Keep 'fix turn 1 first' only if ablation shows flat D3 lift — then sequencing is justified by data, not intuition.
multi_turn.evidence_needed: Controlled A/B: iter-0 baseline prompt, n=20, max_turns ∈ {1,3}, report per-dimension deltas and trigger rate. Turn-2 attribution: on max_turns=3 run, score turn-1 output alone vs final merged report — if final ≫ turn-1, multi-turn is doing real work; if equal, follow-up is theater. Commit-level: flag cases where turn-2 injected blame/history but D3 unchanged — indicates wrong follow-up content, not wrong turn count.

tool_use.builder_position: No runtime tool use; LLM receives pre-assembled context bundle via CommitContextBuilder (diff, message, touched files, numeric features, last-3-commits-per-file history, author stats, router probability). D6=0.85 proves the bundle is sufficient for grounding. Interactive tool use (blame, test discovery, related commits) deferred; reopen if D2 remains stuck after iter-4. Cursor SDK plan mode lacks native tool calling; full agent mode might enable richer investigation but countered by D6 success without tools.
tool_use.evaluator_critique: This is the weakest justified decision in the doc. Equating D6=0.85 with 'no tools needed' conflates citation fidelity with investigative completeness. D6 explicitly catches 'classifies correctly with no evidence' — it does not measure whether the agent found the defect file (D2) or the failure mechanism (D3). D2=0.08 (agent lists all touched files) is unlikely fixed by more prompt text alone; narrowing requires knowing which hunk is causally linked to the fix — blame, test coverage maps, or fix-adjacent file relationships (without oracle leakage) are classic tool paths. D3=0.13 requires inferring runtime behavior; diffs alone are often insufficient for 'missing null check when input empty' unless the diff shows the check removal — many ApacheJIT bugs are integration/logic errors visible only with test or caller context. The builder's turn-2 design already plans 'deeper file history / blame' — that IS tool use, just orchestrator-initiated batch injection rather than LLM-selected tools. The debate is not tools vs no tools; it is deterministic batch tools vs agent-selected tools. Rejecting both until iter-4 is excessive. Cursor plan mode limitation is an implementation constraint being treated as a design validation.
tool_use.recommendation: Reframe tool strategy as 'deterministic context expansion first, agent-selected tools second.' Minimum viable test (cheap, no open agent): extend CommitContextBuilder with opt-in flags — (1) `include_test_files`: if diff touches `src/foo`, inject matching `*Test*` / `test_*` file contents capped at 2K tokens; (2) `include_blame`: for each localized hunk from turn 1 (or all diff hunks if turn 1), inject `git blame -L` snippet. Run n=5 smoke on 2 buggy commits with known D3=0 and D2=0. If zero lift, defer. Full LLM tool use (agent picks blame vs tests) is iter-3+ and only if deterministic expansion plateaus.
tool_use.evidence_needed: n=5 smoke: baseline bundle vs bundle+test files vs bundle+blame vs both, on commits with D6≥0.7 and D3≤0.25. Measure D2 Jaccard and D3 judge score. Track D6 regression and token cost. Document which failure modes each expansion fixes — if test injection fixes behavioral D3 zeros, tools were always the right lever, not iter-4.

overall_philosophy.builder_position: Harness is stable infrastructure; investigation method (prompt, model, turns, context injection) is the variable iterated by the improvement cycle. Eval diagnoses method failures; eval does not fix the agent loop — humans change the method. Hard constraint: no infrastructure/loop changes unless they directly unblock a metric. Separation ensures oracle isolation, reproducibility, and clear attribution of improvements.
overall_philosophy.evaluator_critique: The philosophy is sound as a scientific method for early iterations — hold loop architecture constant, vary prompts, measure D1–D6. But the builder over-applies it. The codebase already contains multi-turn orchestration, follow-up injection, and classification rule checks — that IS loop architecture, not merely 'method.' Declaring 'improvement cycle changes method, not loop' while simultaneously planning iter-3 multi-turn and iter-4 localization focus is inconsistent: turns and context injection are loop variables. Treating loop architecture as fixed risks a local optimum where prompt engineering squeezes D3 from 0.13→0.22 but cannot reach 0.35 because single-turn static bundles cap mechanistic inference on integration defects. The hard constraint 'no infrastructure changes unless they unblock a metric' is backwards — infrastructure changes (bundle expansion, judge split, max_turns in eval) ARE how you unblock metrics. The doc should define explicit pivot triggers: if after iter-1 n=20, ΔD3 <0.05 AND ΔD1 <0.10, loop architecture enters the experimental variable set alongside prompt. Otherwise the team may iterate prompts for weeks against a ceiling imposed by the loop.
overall_philosophy.recommendation: Adopt a two-tier improvement model: Tier 1 (iter-1/2) — method-only changes with loop frozen as documented. Tier 2 (triggered by plateau criteria) — loop architecture becomes a first-class variable: max_turns, deterministic bundle expansion, judge model split, optionally constrained tool palette. Document pivot triggers in state.json: e.g., 'n=20 post-iter-1: target dimension Δ <0.05 → activate Tier 2.' Keep oracle isolation and harness determinism as non-negotiable; everything else is fair game.
overall_philosophy.evidence_needed: Define plateau criteria before iter-1 runs (not after). Track marginal gain per iteration type (prompt-only vs loop change) in breadcrumbs. If prompt-only iterations show diminishing returns (ΔD3 <0.02 between iter-1 and iter-2), that is the signal to promote loop architecture from deferred to active experiment.

consensus: Constrained orchestrator-driven loop is appropriate for V1 cost governance, batch reproducibility, and oracle-safe eval at scale.
Oracle isolation (agent never sees buggy label, fix commit, JIRA) is non-negotiable regardless of loop openness.
Current baseline failure mode is calibration and mechanistic reasoning (D6↑ D3↓ D1↓), not hallucinated evidence.
Same-model investigator+judge is a known risk; rubric-based judging mitigates but does not eliminate self-evaluation bias.
Multi-turn follow-up is implemented in design but untested in eval — activation criteria should be evidence-based.
Prompt/method iteration (iter-1 A+B hybrid) is the lowest-cost first experiment and should run before expensive architectural changes.
D6≥0.70 must remain a regression guard for any loop or method change.
open_questions: What fraction of D3=0 failures are prompt-hedging vs missing test/caller/blame context that no single-turn prompt can fix?
How large is same-model judge leniency on D3/D5 — 5% noise or 15%+ systematic inflation?
Does multi-turn with current follow-up injection (blame + 'what failure mode?') lift D3 materially, or only D1 commitment?
Will deterministic bundle expansion (tests, blame) match or beat agent-selected tool use for D2/D3 at lower cost?
Does a reasoning-heavy model (Opus, o1) lift D3 on the hard subset enough to justify 3–10× turn-1 cost?
Will iter-1 rubric + staged CoT increase follow-up trigger rate (low confidence), inflating multi-turn cost beyond the 40% estimate?
Is D2=0.08 fundamentally a localization prompt problem or a missing defect-locus signal problem solvable only with richer context?

recommended_experiments.description: Re-score n=20 existing investigation reports with cross-model judge (different provider/model than Sonnet investigator). Compare mean D3/D5, rank correlation, and gate pass/fail flip rate vs current same-model scores.
recommended_experiments.decision: If mean D3 drops ≥0.03 or ≥3 commits flip gate status, mandate split judge before n=50 acceptance.

recommended_experiments.description: n=20 stratified eval with iter-0/iter-1 prompt: max_turns=1 vs max_turns=3, identical bundle. Measure ΔD1, ΔD3, ΔD2, cost/commit, follow-up trigger rate. Score turn-1-only output vs final report to attribute lift.
recommended_experiments.decision: If ΔD3≥0.05 or ΔD1≥0.10 with ≤60% cost increase, promote multi-turn to iter-2 track; do not wait for iter-2 failure.

recommended_experiments.description: n=5 smoke on commits with D6≥0.7 and D3≤0.25: (a) baseline bundle, (b) +auto test files, (c) +blame snippets, (d) b+c. No LLM tool selection — orchestrator-only expansion.
recommended_experiments.decision: If (b) or (c) lifts D3≥0.25 on ≥2/5 commits without D6 regression, add to iter-2 context builder before iter-4.

recommended_experiments.description: Select 10 commits with D3=0 and D6≥0.7 from n=100 forensics. Run investigation with Sonnet vs Opus/reasoning model, same prompt. Measure ΔD3 and cost.
recommended_experiments.decision: If Opus ΔD3≥0.15 on subset, consider tiered routing (reasoning model for INVESTIGATE zone only); if flat, stay Sonnet.

recommended_experiments.description: Manual or LLM-assisted tagging of n=50 D3≤0.25 commits into {hedging, generic-structure, missing-context-likely, judge-infra}. Tag drives whether next iteration is method or loop.
recommended_experiments.decision: If >40% tagged missing-context-likely, loop/bundle experiments precede further prompt work.

recommended_experiments.description: On n=20 reports, correlate investigator self-reported confidence with D3 judge score controlling for D6. High residual correlation indicates same-model leniency.
recommended_experiments.decision: If r>0.4, prioritize EXP-JUDGE-SWAP before declaring iter success.
